glossary.def: A parameterised resource address written as an RFC 6570 URI template, such as `file:///{path}`, listed with `resources/templates/list`.
A client feature that told servers which directories and files mattered. Informational, not access control. Deprecated in 2026-07-28.
A client feature that let a server ask the client's model for a completion with `sampling/createMessage`. Deprecated in 2026-07-28.
The remote MCP transport: one endpoint, each JSON-RPC message its own POST, answered with JSON or a per-request SSE stream.
The local MCP transport: the client spawns the server and exchanges newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdin and stdout.
An implementation that supports both legacy `initialize`-based revisions (2025-11-25 and earlier) and modern per-request revisions (2026-07-28 and later).
An opaque string a server returns with `input_required` and the client echoes on retry. It is attacker-controlled input, so integrity must be protected.
Caching hints on discover, list and read results. `ttlMs` is freshness in milliseconds and `cacheScope` is `public` or `private`.
Machine-readable tool output in `structuredContent`, conforming to the tool's `outputSchema`, usually duplicated as text for compatibility.
A tool result block that points to a resource by URI so large data travels by reference instead of inline.
RFC 7591 registration of OAuth clients at runtime. Deprecated in MCP 2026-07-28 in favour of Client ID Metadata Documents.
A server changes a tool description after the user approved it, so an approved tool later carries malicious instructions.
Server-side request forgery: an attacker makes a client or server fetch internal URLs, such as cloud metadata endpoints. MCP OAuth discovery is one exposure.
Loading tool definitions on demand through a search step instead of placing every definition in the model's context.
A Foundry feature that bundles versioned tools behind one governed MCP-compatible endpoint.
Specification Enhancement Proposal, the process maintainers use to change the MCP spec.

claims.text: The Current MCP revision is 2026-07-28, and revisions are YYYY-MM-DD strings that mark the last backwards-incompatible change.
On 2025-12-09 Anthropic donated MCP to the Agentic AI Foundation, a directed fund under the Linux Foundation, and maintainers kept the SEP process.
Tool names SHOULD be 1 to 128 characters from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, underscore, hyphen and dot, and unique per server. Aggregators SHOULD prefix names with a server identifier.
In 2026-07-28, tools/list SHOULD be deterministically ordered, MUST NOT vary per connection and MAY vary by the authorization on the request.
Input validation failures are tool execution errors reported with isError true so the model can self-correct, while unknown tools and malformed requests are JSON-RPC protocol errors.
Resource templates use RFC 6570 URI templates, and completion/complete returns at most 100 items.
In 2026-07-28, resource subscriptions use subscriptions/listen with resourceSubscriptions instead of resources/subscribe, and resource not found changed from -32002 to -32602.
Annotation defaults are readOnlyHint false, destructiveHint true, idempotentHint false and openWorldHint true, and clients MUST treat annotations as untrusted unless they come from trusted servers.
A tool returning structuredContent SHOULD also return the serialized JSON in a TextContent block, and in 2026-07-28 structuredContent may be any JSON value.
Elicitation has form and url modes, and form mode MUST NOT be used for passwords, API keys, access tokens or payment credentials.
In 2026-07-28 elicitation travels inside Multi Round-Trip Requests, notifications/elicitation/complete and elicitationId were removed, and elicitation is not deprecated.
Roots, Sampling and Logging are Deprecated in 2026-07-28 (SEP-2577), with earliest removal in the first revision released on or after 2027-07-28, and no feature has been Removed yet.
Deprecated features stay at least twelve months before removal, or at least ninety days under the expedited-removal exception (SEP-2596).
Agent Framework documentation says sampling removal comes no later than 2027-07-28, which is stricter than the spec's earliest-removal wording.
Roots are informational guidance and the protocol does not enforce that servers stay within them.
MRTR input_required results are allowed only on tools/call, resources/read and prompts/get, and the retry uses a new JSON-RPC id and echoes requestState unchanged.
Servers MUST protect requestState integrity with HMAC or AEAD when it affects authorization or logic, and SHOULD bind principal, expiry and request identity.
The Tasks extension id is io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks with statuses working, input_required, completed, failed and cancelled. tasks/result and tasks/list were removed.
A stdio server MUST NOT write anything but MCP messages to stdout, and stderr is free for logging.
In 2026-07-28 Streamable HTTP, servers MUST validate Origin (403 if invalid) and SHOULD bind local servers to 127.0.0.1.
HTTP+SSE is Deprecated (deprecated since 2025-03-26, reclassified by SEP-2596) and Streamable HTTP replaced it.
2026-07-28 removed the initialize handshake and Mcp-Session-Id. Each request carries protocolVersion and clientCapabilities in _meta, and servers MUST implement server/discover.
An unsupported version returns UnsupportedProtocolVersionError with code -32022 and data.supported and data.requested.
A modern-only server answers legacy GET or DELETE with 405 and ignores Mcp-Session-Id and Last-Event-ID, and a modern client against a legacy-only server fails.
Authorization is optional. HTTP servers SHOULD follow the MCP authorization spec, while stdio servers SHOULD NOT and instead retrieve credentials from the environment.

Servers MUST implement RFC 9728 protected resource metadata with at least one authorization_servers entry, advertised by resource_metadata in the 401 WWW-Authenticate header or at /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource.
Clients MUST use PKCE with S256 and MUST refuse to proceed if code_challenge_methods_supported is absent from the authorization server metadata.
Clients MUST send the RFC 8707 resource parameter in authorization and token requests, and MCP servers MUST validate that tokens were issued for them.
Clients SHOULD try registration in order: pre-registered credentials, Client ID Metadata Documents, Dynamic Client Registration (Deprecated), then ask the user.
Token passthrough is forbidden: MCP servers MUST NOT accept tokens not explicitly issued for them or transit other tokens.

The confused deputy attack needs a static client ID, dynamic client registration, a third-party consent cookie and no per-client consent. Consent cookies MUST use the __Host- prefix, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, be signed and be bound to client_id.
Invariant Labs named tool poisoning attacks and rug pulls on 2025-04-01. They are not defined in the MCP spec.
MCP SSRF mitigations include HTTPS enforcement, blocking private and link-local ranges such as 169.254.0.0/16, validating redirect targets and using an egress proxy.

MCP client guidance suggests switching to progressive tool discovery at a threshold such as 1% to 5% of the context window and illustrates about 150,000 tokens of definitions versus about 2,000 on demand.

Anthropic reports about 55k tokens of definitions for a five-server setup, over 85 percent saved with tool search, accuracy degrading past 30 to 50 tools, and advises tool search at 10 or more tools or over 10k definition tokens.
Adding or removing tool definitions mid-conversation invalidates the prompt cache, so append discovered definitions after the cache breakpoint or route calls through a stable call_tool wrapper.
API Management MCP support covers tools only, not resources or prompts, is not supported in workspaces, and policies apply to all tools in a server.
Foundry Toolbox exposes a versioned tool bundle at one MCP-compatible endpoint. Tool search and skills are Preview as of 2026-10-13, and a first OAuth use can return CONSENT_REQUIRED (-32006).
The official MCP Registry is Preview, public only, not designed for self-hosting, and host apps should consume downstream registries instead of calling it directly.
Foundry OpenAPI tools use OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1, require an operationId per operation, and support anonymous, API key and managed identity authentication.
